_about: The After Hours Library: the home page as a game library. One title per part of the resume, each with key art, its own score layer, stats and trophies. Every trophy is a verified fact from llms.txt, and every line here must already be in llms.txt. assemble_home.py renders this into plain HTML (crawlers and screen readers read it as a document); game.js only arranges and reveals it. No em dashes, no percent signs, first person for what Jason did.

overview: I designed the lead-to-title data model, roles and validation, and tested Supabase RLS policies to prevent unauthorized role access.
I added validation that prevents invalid deal and inventory records from being written.
I executed production schema migrations while preserving existing records and operational tables.

Its sale desk, Handle a Sale, asks one plain question at a time, scans the buyer's license once so every form fills itself, does the registration math, and routes the deal to the right documents. It works in English or Spanish, and the customer signs on their phone or in person.
